proof:
Notation. mu := V.weight, p_y := V.tangentProj y, P_T := T.starProjection, f(y) := hsNormSq(p_y - P_T), B_s := closedBall zeta s, E(s) := V.tiltExcess zeta s T = (s^n)^(-1) * (Bochner integral of f over B_s). (L8), (L9) are from la_basics.

1. Uniform bound. By the definition of tangentProj, for every y either p_y = K.starProjection for some linear subspace K of R^(n+l) (the chosen approximate tangent space) or p_y = 0. In the first case hsNormSq(p_y) <= n + l by (L9) with m = n + l; in the second, hsNormSq(p_y) = 0. Also hsNormSq(P_T) <= n + l by (L9), so hsNormSq(-P_T) <= n + l by (L8d). By (L8c) with M = p_y and N = -P_T, and by (L8a): 0 <= f(y) <= 2(n + l) + 2(n + l) = 4(n + l) for every y.

2. A.e. strong measurability. Phi : M -> hsNormSq(M - P_T), on the finite-dimensional normed space of continuous linear maps of R^(n+l), is continuous: it is a finite sum of squares of norms of the continuous maps M -> (M - P_T)e_i. Since y -> p_y is mu-a.e. strongly measurable, so is f = Phi o p, with respect to mu and to every restriction of mu.

3. Integrability. If mu(B_s) < infinity, then f is a.e. strongly measurable and bounded by 4(n + l) on B_s, a set of finite measure. So f is mu-integrable on B_s.

4. (T1). Let s > 0 with mu(B_s) < infinity. By step 3 and f >= 0, the identity for nonnegative integrable functions gives ofReal(integral_{B_s} f d mu) = lower integral over B_s of ofReal(f) d mu. Since s > 0, s^n > 0, so s^n E(s) = s^n (s^n)^(-1) integral_{B_s} f d mu = integral_{B_s} f d mu. Hence the lower integral equals ofReal(s^n E(s)).

5. (T2). Let 0 < sigma <= s with mu(B_s) < infinity. As in step 4, sigma^n E(sigma) = integral_{B_sigma} f d mu and s^n E(s) = integral_{B_s} f d mu. Now B_sigma is contained in B_s, f is integrable on B_s (step 3) and f >= 0. Monotonicity of set integrals of nonnegative integrable functions in the domain gives integral_{B_sigma} f d mu <= integral_{B_s} f d mu.

6. (T3). For s > 0, (s^n)^(-1) > 0. Also integral_{B_s} f d mu >= 0 because f >= 0 everywhere; a Bochner integral of a nonnegative function is nonnegative, and it is 0 when the function is not integrable. Hence E(s) >= 0.
key_steps: Every tangentProj value is an orthogonal projection or 0, so hsNormSq(p_y) <= n+l and 0 <= f <= 4(n+l)
f is a continuous function of the a.e. strongly measurable tangentProj, hence integrable on balls of finite measure
